1.summary: Paul, in chains, remembers Timothy's tears and his sincere faith passed down from his grandmother and mother, urges him to rekindle his gift and not be ashamed of the gospel or of Paul, to guard the good deposit, and mentions those who deserted him and Onesiphorus who did not.
1.lookfor: Notice the generations of faith, and the contrast between those ashamed of Paul and Onesiphorus.

names.name: Timothy
names.gloss: Paul's beloved son in the faith.

names.name: Lois
names.gloss: Timothy's grandmother.

names.name: Eunice
names.gloss: Timothy's mother, a Jewish believer.

names.name: Phygelus
names.gloss: One of those in Asia who turned away from Paul.

names.name: Hermogenes
names.gloss: Another who turned away.

names.name: Onesiphorus
names.gloss: A friend who searched Rome for Paul and wasn't ashamed of his chains.

insights.title: Your tears
insights.body: Paul remembers Timothy's tears (1:4), probably at their last parting. This is a letter between close friends.

insights.title: Faith in the family
insights.body: The sincere faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and mother Eunice now lives in you (1:5). Timothy was taught the Scriptures from childhood.

insights.title: Fan into flame
insights.body: Stir up the gift of God which is in you (1:6). The verb means to rekindle a fire that's burning low.

insights.title: Not a spirit of fear
insights.body: God didn't give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love and self-control (1:7). Timothy may have been timid; Paul reminds him what the Spirit supplies.

insights.title: Ashamed of a prisoner
insights.body: Being associated with a condemned prisoner was dangerous and shameful in Rome. Many in Asia abandoned Paul, but Onesiphorus searched diligently until he found him (1:15-17).

insights.title: Guard the deposit
insights.body: Guard the good deposit entrusted to you by the Holy Spirit (1:14). The gospel is like valuables left in safekeeping, to be kept intact and handed on.

insights.title: Not ashamed
insights.body: Paul says I'm not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed (1:12). Where are you tempted to keep quiet about your faith?

2.summary: Paul urges Timothy to entrust the teaching to faithful people, to endure hardship like a soldier, athlete and farmer, to remember Jesus raised from the dead, to handle the word rightly, avoid quarrels, flee youthful passions and gently correct opponents.
2.lookfor: Notice the three pictures of endurance, and the chain of four generations in verse 2.

names.name: David
names.gloss: Israel's king, ancestor of Jesus.

names.name: Hymenaeus
names.gloss: A teacher who said the resurrection had already happened.

names.name: Philetus
names.gloss: Hymenaeus's fellow false teacher.

insights.title: Four generations
insights.body: What you heard from me, entrust to faithful people who will be able to teach others also (2:2): Paul, Timothy, faithful people, others. The gospel is passed hand to hand.

insights.title: Soldier, athlete, farmer
insights.body: A soldier doesn't get entangled in civilian affairs, an athlete competes by the rules, a hardworking farmer gets the first share of the crop (2:4-6). Single focus, discipline, patient labor.

insights.title: The word isn't chained
insights.body: I suffer hardship to the point of chains as a criminal, but God's word isn't chained (2:9). The messenger is bound; the message is free.

insights.title: He remains faithful
insights.body: If we are faithless, he remains faithful, for he can't deny himself (2:13). This faithful saying ends not with our faithfulness but with his.

insights.title: Rightly dividing
insights.body: Handle correctly the word of truth (2:15). The verb means to cut straight, like a road builder or a tentmaker cutting cloth accurately.

insights.title: The Lord knows his own
insights.body: God's firm foundation bears this seal: the Lord knows those who are his (2:19), from Numbers 16, where God distinguished the faithful from Korah's rebels.

insights.title: Gentle correction
insights.body: The Lord's servant must not quarrel but be gentle, patiently correcting opponents, in case God grants them repentance (2:24-25). The goal is rescue, not winning.

insights.title: Passing it on
insights.body: Paul wanted the faith passed to people who would pass it on again. Who are you investing in who could one day teach others?

3.summary: Paul warns that in the last days people will be lovers of self and money, having a form of godliness but denying its power; he reminds Timothy of his own sufferings and that all who live godly will be persecuted, and urges him to continue in the Scriptures, which are God-breathed and equip for every good work.
3.lookfor: Notice the list of vices that begins and ends with love of the wrong things, and what Scripture is useful for.

names.name: Jannes
names.gloss: By Jewish tradition, one of Pharaoh's magicians who opposed Moses.

names.name: Jambres
names.gloss: The other magician named in tradition.

names.name: Antioch
names.gloss: Pisidian Antioch, where Paul was persecuted on his first journey.

names.name: Iconium
names.gloss: Where Paul faced a plot to stone him.

names.name: Lystra
names.gloss: Timothy's hometown, where Paul was stoned.

insights.title: Lovers of the wrong things
insights.body: People will be lovers of self, lovers of money, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God (3:2-4). The list is bracketed by misdirected love.

insights.title: A form of godliness
insights.body: Having a form of godliness but denying its power (3:5). The word is morphōsis, an outward shape. Religious appearance without transformation.

insights.title: Jannes and Jambres
insights.body: As Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses (3:8). Exodus doesn't name Pharaoh's magicians; their names come from Jewish tradition, which Paul draws on.

insights.title: What happened at Lystra
insights.body: Paul reminds Timothy of persecutions at Antioch, Iconium and Lystra (3:11). Timothy, from Lystra, may have seen Paul stoned there.

insights.title: All who live godly
insights.body: All who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will be persecuted (3:12). Hostility isn't a sign something has gone wrong.

insights.title: God-breathed
insights.body: All Scripture is inspired by God, theopneustos, God-breathed (3:16). Scripture comes from God's own breath, as he breathed life into Adam.

insights.title: Equipped for every good work
insights.body: Scripture is profitable for teaching, reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness, so God's servant is complete, equipped for every good work (3:16-17). Its goal is a changed life.

insights.title: From childhood
insights.body: Timothy knew the Scriptures from childhood (3:15). What would help Scripture become more familiar to you, or to the children in your life?

4.summary: Paul solemnly charges Timothy to preach the word in season and out, because people will want teachers who tell them what they want to hear; facing death, he says he has finished the race and kept the faith, asks Timothy to come quickly and bring his cloak and books, and tells how the Lord stood by him when everyone deserted him.
4.lookfor: Notice Paul's calm in facing death, and the very human requests: a cloak, books, friends.

names.name: Demas
names.gloss: A co-worker who left Paul, loving this present world.

names.name: Crescens
names.gloss: A co-worker who went to Galatia.

names.name: Dalmatia
names.gloss: A region on the Adriatic coast (modern Croatia).

names.name: Luke
names.gloss: The physician who alone stayed with Paul.

names.name: Mark
names.gloss: Once a dropout, now useful to Paul for ministry.

names.name: Troas
names.gloss: Where Paul left his cloak with Carpus.

names.name: Alexander
names.gloss: A coppersmith who did Paul much harm.

names.name: Trophimus
names.gloss: A co-worker left sick at Miletus.

insights.title: In season and out
insights.body: Preach the word; be ready in season and out of season (4:2), when it's welcome and when it isn't.

insights.title: Itching ears
insights.body: People will heap up teachers to suit their own desires, having itching ears (4:3). Popular speakers in Greek cities were judged by how much they pleased crowds.

insights.title: Poured out
insights.body: I am already being poured out as a drink offering (4:6). Wine was poured out over sacrifices; Paul sees his coming death as an offering to God.

insights.title: Finished the race
insights.body: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith (4:7). Waiting for him is the crown of righteousness, and not for him only, but for all who have loved Christ's appearing (4:8).

insights.title: The cloak and the parchments
insights.body: Bring the cloak I left at Troas, and the books, especially the parchments (4:13). Winter in a Roman prison was cold; even at the end, Paul wanted to read.

insights.title: Mark again
insights.body: Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry (4:11). The young man Paul once refused is now wanted at his side.

insights.title: The Lord stood with me
insights.body: At my first defense no one came to support me, but the Lord stood with me and strengthened me (4:16-17). Paul echoes Jesus' prayer: may it not be held against them.

insights.title: Finishing
insights.body: Paul could look back and say he'd kept the faith. What would you want to be able to say at the end of your race?

intro.who: The letter names Paul, writing to Timothy from prison in Rome as he faces death (1:8, 4:6). As with 1 Timothy, some scholars think a follower wrote it in Paul's name; its warm personal details lead many to think it is Paul's.
intro.when: If by Paul, about AD 64–67, during a second, harsher Roman imprisonment under Nero, shortly before his execution.
intro.why: It reads like Paul's last will: he urges Timothy not to be ashamed, to guard the gospel, endure hardship, hold to Scripture and preach the word, and to come to him quickly before winter.
